newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips rebound at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips rebound at close.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks bounced back at the close in rising volume Monday, erasing sharp early losses on the back of a similar turnaround on Wall Street, dealers said.

"The market was very nervous today about Wall Street's performance, and in the end it enjoyed a recovery," said dealer Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "Tomorrow everything depends on the U.S. consumer inflation report and how it affects the markets."
The blue-chip MerVal index recovered from a low of 670.86 to close at 689.54 with a 0.5 percent rise.

"The 700 mark used to be a floor, but now it may become a resistance level," another trader said. "It depends whether the New York markets keep steady tomorrow -- if so, we could manage a stronger recovery."
Floor volume remained modest but swelled to 20.4 million pesos from 15.9 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover was unchanged at 77 million pesos.
The broad market pared losses but still closed off 0.4 percent, with decliners beating risers 33 to 14 and 13 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Sevel and oil company Astra, which rallied 3.8 percent, 3.0 percent and 2.8 percent, respectively. MerVal losers included Telefonica and Telecom, off 2.4 percent and 1.6 percent, and construction stock Polledo, down 1.9 percent.

A second-line stock, Pepsi bottler Baesa, staged a 10 percent technical rebound after plunging nearly 40 percent in two sessions on its dire financial outlook. Baesa said late Friday it was considering the sale of its Chilean assets and exploring alliances in Argentina and Brazil.
